beats.narration_slice: Metal bones could carry heavy loads.
beats.visual: A paper-cut human skeleton with metallic bone sections lifting a large stone weight in a warm anatomical workshop landscape, showing increased carrying capacity.
beats.purpose: show that metal structures can support heavy loads
beats.visual_fingerprint: silver metal-boned skeleton standing in an orchard clearing while lifting a massive stone, low angle close composition with amber light
beats.continuity: begin the topic world with a full-body skeleton comparison scene

beats.narration_slice: Joints need movement, not only strength.
beats.visual: A close paper-cut view of a knee and elbow joint made from layered bone and soft tissue pieces, bending smoothly beside a rigid metal hinge comparison.
beats.purpose: show that joints require flexibility and motion
beats.visual_fingerprint: close-up knee joint comparison with flexible living layers and stiff metal hinge pieces on a mossy ground setting, side angle
beats.continuity: move from skeleton strength to the mechanics of movement

beats.narration_slice: Real bones are strong and slightly bendable.
beats.visual: A natural bone structure made from cream paper layers gently flexing like a living branch while maintaining its shape.
beats.purpose: show the combination of strength and slight flexibility in real bones
beats.visual_fingerprint: cream anatomical bone arching gently like a branch in a sunlit orchard biome, medium shot from above
beats.continuity: continue from joint motion into the qualities of living bone

beats.narration_slice: Metal frames bend less than bones.
beats.visual: A split visual of a flexible bone-like structure curving and a metal frame resisting the same bending force.
beats.purpose: compare flexibility between bone and metal structures
beats.visual_fingerprint: two vertical structures in a paper-cut laboratory grove, one curved cream bone and one rigid slate metal frame under side lighting
beats.continuity: shift from natural bone properties to direct material comparison

beats.narration_slice: The body could become too heavy to move.
beats.visual: A full-body silhouette with oversized metallic bones struggling to take a step through soft grass, showing weight affecting movement.
beats.purpose: show how heavier metal bones could make movement difficult
beats.visual_fingerprint: tiny human figure with oversized silver skeletal frame trudging through tall orchard grass, wide shot with downward camera angle
beats.continuity: move from material stiffness to whole-body consequences

beats.narration_slice: Muscles may struggle with a heavier skeleton.
beats.visual: Layered paper muscles around a metallic skeleton pulling with effort as the body attempts to lift an arm.
beats.purpose: show that muscles would face extra demands from a heavier skeleton
beats.visual_fingerprint: anatomical muscle layers straining around a silver skeleton in a shaded woodland clearing, close three-quarter view
beats.continuity: continue the weight problem by focusing on body systems

beats.narration_slice: Metal bones could make repairs harder after damage.
beats.visual: A damaged metallic bone section with complicated repair pieces and tools compared with a simpler living bone healing scene.
beats.purpose: show that repairing metal bone replacements could be difficult
beats.visual_fingerprint: broken silver bone structure surrounded by layered repair fragments on a warm medical workbench environment, top-down composition
beats.continuity: follow body strain into repair challenges

beats.narration_slice: Medical parts called implants use titanium for support.
beats.visual: A realistic paper-cut medical implant piece made of titanium placed beside a human bone, showing a small supportive role.
beats.purpose: show that titanium implants are used as supportive medical parts
beats.visual_fingerprint: small titanium implant beside cream bone layers in a calm clinic garden setting, focused close composition with soft amber highlights
beats.continuity: transition from repair problems to real medical uses of metal

beats.narration_slice: They do not replace a whole living skeleton.
beats.visual: A complete living skeleton with one small titanium implant area highlighted by placement and scale contrast.
beats.purpose: show that implants are limited parts rather than a complete metal skeleton replacement
beats.visual_fingerprint: full human skeleton with one tiny silver support piece in a botanical anatomy space, distant centered composition
beats.continuity: clarify the difference between support parts and total replacement

beats.narration_slice: A strong skeleton must help the body move and work well.
beats.visual: A balanced human skeleton walking and reaching naturally while surrounded by flowing muscle and movement shapes.
beats.purpose: show that a useful skeleton must combine strength with movement
beats.visual_fingerprint: healthy cream skeleton moving through an orchard path with flowing muscle layers, dynamic full-body side composition
beats.continuity: bring together strength, flexibility and function as the conclusion of the body explanation

beats.narration_slice: Metal gives strength, but it can also cause movement problems.
beats.visual: A final balanced comparison showing a strong metal piece beside a flexible living skeleton moving freely.
beats.purpose: reinforce the tradeoff between metal strength and movement limitations
beats.visual_fingerprint: split-depth orchard anatomy scene with rigid silver structure on one side and moving living skeleton on the other, wide final composition
beats.continuity: final reflection staying inside the topic world
